title: Stolen 120-year-old church bell found discarded in rural Manitoba ditch
summary: A heavy church bell stolen from the top of a belfry in rural Manitoba has been found abandoned in a ditch.

image.caption: RCMP Const. Merry Ploeg stands with the recovered church bell in the back of a police pickup truck on Tuesday. (Karen Pauls/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba
A heavy church bell stolen from the top of a belfry in rural Manitoba has been found abandoned in a ditch.
'Now we can kind of shift our focus over to figuring out who took it and how': RCMP
RCMP recovered it around 5:30 a.m. Tuesday near the small community of Malonton after receiving a tip from a passerby.
It was dumped about 10 kilometres southwest of the Sacred Heart of Jesus Ukrainian Catholic Church, which is 80 kilometres north of Winnipeg near Fraserwood.
It was stolen from the church during the week leading up to Nov. 14, when the theft was discovered, police said.
"That was a really unique piece of history, and we're just really relieved that it's been recovered and it's in good condition. It appears to be mostly undamaged," said RCMP Const. Merry Ploeg.
"Now we can kind of shift our focus over to figuring out who took it and how they took it. Even just recovering it took a few people, so it's quite a heavy piece of history."
Damage can be seen at the top of the wooden belfry. (Tyler Searle/CBC)

The bell, estimated to weigh about 135 kilograms (300 pounds), was somehow removed from a 1½-storey belfry that stands at the back of the Sacred Heart of Jesus churchyard in Manitoba's Interlake region.
Some boards were broken and removed from the top of the belfry, but how it was lowered is a mystery.
"That one … I haven't quite figured it out," said Ploeg.
There’s nothing on the ground to indicate where it might have landed if it was pushed out, and there are no tracks from any vehicles.

"I went over there and I was going over it pretty thoroughly just because, personally, I'd like to see if there's any cigarette butts left behind or anything that we could use as evidence. And I really wasn't finding anything," Ploeg said.
The bell from the Sacred Heart of Jesus Church is estimated to weigh more than 130 kilograms. Manitoba RCMP are still trying to figure out who took it and how. (Submitted by RCMP)
It was spotted in a ditch along Road 12 East by someone heading out to their hunting spot, she said.
Ploeg and the church parishioners were worried the ornate brass bell, which dates back to 1906, had been stolen to be sold to a scrapyard or melted down.
All the media attention the theft garnered likely scared the thieves off, said Ploeg, who believes they left it in a place where it could be found "so that they could get the heat off of them."

"Typically when we recover stolen property it'll be quite well hidden in the bushes or on properties, like rural areas, where people will stash them and wait until they can either use them or dispose of them another way or sell them or whatever," she said.

"The way that the bell was abandoned just in the ditch on the side of the road in plain view makes me feel very much that it was, like, purposeful. It wasn't stashed. It was left there to be found because now it's a hot item and it's all over the news."
The original church was built in Fraserwood in 1906. The current building was erected in 1942, two years after the original one was destroyed by a fire. (Tyler Searle/CBC)
The Interlake has large swaths of bushland and uninhabited areas where the thieves could have hidden the bell, Ploeg said.
"Even if you had a drone, what are the odds of you spotting it? It's the exact same colour as the grass [right now in fall]," she said.

items: 120-year-old church bell weighing 300 pounds stolen from belfry in rural Manitoba

blocks.text: The bell is now with the RCMP's forensics unit, which will be looking for fingerprints or other evidence that can be gathered from it.
Ploeg has spoken with representatives of the church to let them know it's been found.
The church isn't ready to take it back, anyway, because they need to do some repairs to the top of the belfry, where some of the wood was damaged during the theft, she said.
"So we'll give them some time to kind of figure that out and we'll make a plan of how it's going to be returned."
Gimli RCMP ask anyone with information about the theft or who may have seen anything suspicious in the area to contact the detachment at 204-642-5106.
